help.title: help
body: HOW TO READ THE NUMBERS
• Dedicated VRAM — bytes of the process resident in the card's physical memory
(the 'Local Usage' counter). This is what actually occupies the VRAM.
• Shared — bytes that spilled over into system RAM ('Non Local Usage').
Part of the GPU memory total, but it does not occupy physical VRAM.
• Total GPU — dedicated + shared. This is Task Manager's 'GPU memory'.
• Committed — everything the process reserved ('Total Committed'), including
blocks shared between processes and paged-out blocks. The sum across all
processes can exceed the physical total, because a shared allocation is
counted in every process that references it — which is why dwm.exe sometimes
shows up with tens of GB. Do not use this column to decide who is filling
the VRAM.
• GPU / Engine — utilization of the busiest engine (3D, Compute, Copy,
VideoDecode...).
• Bottom panel — the blocks per physical segment of the adapter, which is as
granular as Windows gets without kernel ETW tracing.
SAFETY WHEN ENDING PROCESSES
• CRITICAL — ending it causes a blue screen or drops the session (System,
csrss, lsass, winlogon, services...). The monitor blocks the action.
• System — SYSTEM/service account or session 0. Requires explicit confirmation
and shows which services go down with it.
• Elevated — administrator token. May require the monitor to be elevated, or UAC.
• User — ordinary process of your session.
SHORTCUTS
Del  end             Ctrl+C  copy taskkill        F5  refresh
Space  pause         Ctrl+F  filter               F1  this help
Double-clicking a row opens the confirmation dialog.
LIST AND SORTING
While the pointer is over the list, or the scroll is away from the top, the
order freezes: values keep updating, but rows stop swapping places so you can
read them. Go back to the top and move the mouse away to resume live ranking.
TRAY AND HEADLESS BRIDGE
The close button (X) minimizes to the notification area and the monitor keeps
running; the icon shows the dedicated VRAM percentage. Use 'Exit' in the tray
menu to quit for real.
On every sample the app writes a full JSON snapshot to:
That is the headless bridge: any script (or agent) can read that file without
needing the window. It can be toggled in the tray menu.
With no window at all, the command line does the same:
VramMonitor.exe --json            one snapshot on stdout
VramMonitor.exe --text            readable table
VramMonitor.exe --watch           one JSON per line, continuous
VramMonitor.exe --headless        no window, just keeping the file fresh
VramMonitor.exe --kill PID        ends a process with the same safeguards
VramMonitor.exe --help            every option
The tray menu also has **Start with Windows**: it first tries the common startup
folder for all users (asks for UAC) and, if elevation is refused, offers to install
only for your user, which needs no elevation at all.
LANGUAGES
English, Portuguese, Spanish, French and German ship inside the executable.
To add or override one, drop a JSON file in:
Copy one of the files from the repository's lang/ folder as a starting point;
a file with the same meta.code replaces the built-in one. Missing keys fall
back to English.
